Based on the search results, here's what I found about Florhydral from Givaudan:

## Overview

Florhydral is a synthetic aliphatic aldehyde developed by Givaudan. It is classified chemically as a substituted benzenepropanal with a bulky isopropyl substituent at the meta-position of the phenyl ring.

## Olfactory Profile

Florhydral has a very floral, fresh, natural odour (such as lily of the valley, hyacinth). Its great intensity and pleasant quality make it useful in all areas of perfumery. Florhydral is also valuable in fragrances for laundry products where a fresh residual odour is desired.

## Chemical Properties

The chemical name is 3-(3-Isopropylphenyl)butanal with formula C13H18O, molecular weight 190.3, and CAS # 125109-85-5.

## Development

Florhydral was developed by Givaudan during the late 20th century and was first disclosed in US Patent 4,910,346, filed by A. Chalk for Givaudan Corporation and published on November 10, 1988.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Florhydral (CAS 125109-85-5):

## Overview
Florhydral® (CAS N° 125109-85-5) is an ingredient used in perfumes. Its chemical name is 3-(3-Isopropylphenyl)butanal with molecular formula C13H18O and molecular weight of 190.28.

## Properties and Appearance
Florhydral is a colorless to pale yellow clear liquid with an intensely floral aroma, featuring notes reminiscent of muguet, linden flower, and lily of the valley.

## Applications
Florhydral® is generally used to create lily of the valley or hyacinth notes and is especially used for reformulating Lilial®-containing perfumes. Its great intensity and pleasant quality make it useful in all areas of perfumery, and it is also valuable in fragrances for laundry products where a fresh residual odour is desired.

## Usage Levels
Recommended usage is 0.2-2% with tenacity of about one week on a smelling strip, and this material also works well in burning applications such as candles and joss sticks.

## Synthesis
Florhydral® can be synthesized by a hydroformylation reaction of 1,3-diisopropenylbenzene, using carbon monoxide and hydrogen to form an aldehydic group, starting from an alkene group.

Based on the search results, here's information about Florhydral safety data sheets:

## Overview
Florhydral (also known as 3-(3-Isopropylphenyl)butanal with CAS number 125109-85-5) is a fragrance ingredient used in perfumery and personal care products.

## Safety Profile
Florhydral demonstrates a favorable safety profile for cosmetic and perfumery applications when used according to good manufacturing practices and recommended dosage guidelines. Florhydral is not listed among the EU's 26 declarable fragrance allergens, meaning it does not require individual declaration on cosmetic product labels.

## Handling Precautions
Safety data sheets typically indicate that Florhydral should be handled with care, as it may pose health risks if ingested or inhaled, and appropriate personal protective equipment should be used during handling.

First-aid measures include removing from exposure to fresh air and keeping at rest with medical attention; for inhalation, flush immediately with water for at least 15 minutes.

For storage, keep in a well-ventilated place, keep container tightly closed, and keep cool.

Safety data sheets for Florhydral are available from various suppliers including Vigon International, Givaudan, and other chemical suppliers.

Based on the search results, here's information about Florhydral use levels:

## Use Level Guidelines

The recommended use level for Florhydral is 0.2% - 2%. More specifically, it is normally used at less than 1% of the concentrate except in Lily of the Valley applications.

For those new to working with this ingredient, it's recommended to begin testing at 0.5–1% in simple floral bases to understand its character before incorporating into complex compositions.

## Performance Notes

Florhydral is remarkably powerful yet refined, effective at concentrations as low as 0.5% in fragrance concentrates, yet never overwhelming. It has a tenacity of about one week on a smelling strip and works well in burning applications such as candles and joss sticks.

## Key Characteristics

At low dosages, it adds crisp, clean freshness; at higher levels, it becomes distinctly hyacinth-like.

Based on the search results, here's information about Florhydral's odor and vapor pressure:

## Odor Characteristics

Florhydral is a synthetic aldehyde used in perfumery for its floral-green lily-of-the-valley scent. It is described as having a floral, green, muguet, fresh, and powerful odor.

The odor potency varies by enantiomer: The (+)-(S)-enantiomer exhibits a more pronounced green, less watery character with greater power and an odor threshold of 0.035 ng/L air.

## Vapor Pressure

Florhydral has a vapor pressure of 0.02 hPa, which gives it medium volatility and allows it to function as a heart note in fragrance composition. The vapor pressure at 20°C is specifically noted as 0.0200 hPa.

These properties make Florhydral suitable for use in various perfumery applications where a lasting floral character is desired.
